change: Replaced first-party libc access and chmod unsafe blocks with safe rustix wrappers; retained the existing C-string conversion and all input mode bits.

dependency.source_evidence: src/fs/abs.rs delegates access/chmod to the selected backend. src/backend/libc/fs/syscalls.rs calls libc access/chmod once and returns the OS error without a retry loop.
dependency.mode_conversion: Mode::from_raw_mode strips S_IFMT; from_bits_retain preserves the original cast-to-mode_t behavior instead.
dependency.trust: Established dependency unsafe is separately trusted and inventoried; this is not a claim that rustix contains no unsafe. No custom first-party implementation was moved into the dependency.
dependency.feature_unification: use-libc also selects rustix's libc backend for other users of the same package, including tempfile; full workspace tests and native validation must cover this shared feature selection.
dependency.policy_checks: cargo deny --all-features check and cargo audit passed

compatibility.fixtures: Three Linux tests passed before and after replacement: all access combinations, first-NUL truncation, non-ASCII paths, chmod through symlinks, permission bits, and ENOENT/ENOTDIR cases.
compatibility.source_contract: Both paths continue through c_path, preserve libc constants and raw errno, and use the same libc entrypoints. No public signature, trait bound or package version changed.
compatibility.limits: Fixtures do not simulate interrupted syscalls or alternate real/effective credentials. One-shot behavior and use of access rather than effective-credential access are established by inspected pinned backend source. Native cross-platform runs remain pending.

deletion: Deleted both selected unsafe blocks directly; no parallel legacy access/chmod implementation remains.
inventory: Source blocks 17 to 15; expected native_unix compiler spans Linux 32 to 28 and macOS 28 to 24. Windows unchanged. Full compiler verification pending.
migration_limit: Direct replacement in this increment, within the current migration milestone.
exclusions: No Miri claim for system calls
